title: Fields and properties
hook: Fields store state. Properties are methods in a costume: get, set, and init accessors that you can version without turning every caller into a field-access rewrite. C# 14’s field keyword is the backing store you no longer have to name.

sections.heading: Fields stay private
sections.prose: A field is storage. Public fields freeze the binary shape: you cannot add validation, lazy creation, or change-notification later without breaking callers. Constants are compile-time values; static readonly is a runtime one-time assignment. Instance fields plus a constructor (next topics) are how a cache entry or auth ticket holds data. Encapsulation here is not style — the CLR will refuse private access from other types.

sections.heading: get, set, and init
sections.prose: get returns the value. set assigns after the object exists — fine for a worker’s retry counter, wrong for an auth token you want frozen after construction. init is a setter that is only legal during construction: a constructor body or an object initializer. Auto-properties ({ get; set; } or { get; init; }) still have a hidden backing field. Expression-bodied accessors are the same members with shorter syntax.

snippets.label: C# 14 field-backed property with validation
snippets.explanation: field is the compiler-synthesized backing field. You write validation in set without declaring _payload. Key uses init plus required so callers must supply it in an initializer.

sections.heading: The field keyword and name clashes
sections.prose: In C# 14, inside an accessor, the contextual keyword field means the synthesized backing field. You can body get, set, or both. Patterns that used to need a manual field — null-coalescing lazy init, trimming strings, raising PropertyChanged — collapse into the property. If the type already has a member named field, the keyword can change meaning; Microsoft documents @field or this.field as disambiguation, or you rename the old member. This is a real upgrade-time gotcha when moving a codebase to C# 14 / .NET 10.

interviewTakeaways: Properties are the versionable API; fields are implementation.
init is not immutable forever — it only restricts assignment to construction. with on records (module 05) copies into a new instance.
C# 14 field removes most manual backing fields; watch for identifier collisions.
commonPitfalls: Public mutable fields on DTOs that later need validation.
Assuming { get; init; } makes a class safe to share across threads — it does not add synchronization.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JS getters/setters are similar in spirit but remain a prototype/object feature without CLR accessibility. There is no init accessor.
TS constructor(public name: string) creates a field. C# primary constructors plus properties are explicit about backing storage and init versus set.
